**RE: Member Appeal of Prior Authorization Denial**
*   **Member Name:** Rowan Delgado
*   **Member ID:** W865123628
*   **Plan:** Blue Cross Blue Shield of North Dakota (Commercial/ACA)
*   **Reference Number:** POC-9391F374E1-41425
*   **Requested Service:** Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion (ACDF)
*   **Procedure Code (CPT):** 22551
*   **Ordering Provider:** Dr. Marchetti, MD (Orthopedic Surgery)

Dear Appeals Committee,

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for the anterior cervical discectomy and fusion (ACDF) surgery prescribed by my surgeon, Dr. Marchetti, MD. 

The denial notice dated August 18, 2026, states that the requested procedure "does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity." However, a review of my clinical history against the BCBSND Medical Policy **"Cervical Fusions" (Policy ID: S-9004-02, Revision Effective Date: July 01, 2024)** demonstrates that I completely satisfy every medical necessity criterion required for this procedure. 

Under the policy section **"ANTERIOR CERVICAL FUSION FOR DEGENERATIVE DISEASE"**, single or multilevel ACDF (CPT 22551) is considered medically necessary when three specific conditions are met. Below, I have mapped my clinical and diagnostic records directly to these requirements to prove medical necessity:

### 1. Radiculopathy and Refractory Conservative Management
*   **BCBSND Policy Criterion:** 
    > *"unremitting cervical radiculopathy and/or myelopathy (i.e., neck and arm pain) resulting in disability and/or neurological deficit that are refractory to at least six weeks of standard conservative, nonoperative management (e.g., reduced activities, exercise, analgesics, physical therapy), in the absence of progressive or severe myelopathy"*
*   **Clinical Mapping:** 
    *   **Unremitting Radiculopathy & Deficit:** I have suffered from 14 months of progressive, unremitting neck pain that is unrelieved by rest. This has resulted in significant disability and neurological deficit, specifically radicular pain, numbness, and weakness radiating into my right thumb and index finger.
    *   **Conservative Care:** My condition has proven completely refractory to intensive conservative management. I completed **8 weeks of supervised physical therapy** (exceeding the 6-week policy requirement) from May 18, 2026, to July 13, 2026. This comprised **18 total visits** focusing on cervical traction and postural training, as documented in my physical therapy discharge note. 
    *   **Medications:** I have taken NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate pain relief. Additionally, I underwent a cervical corticosteroid injection on May 8, 2026, which provided only 3 weeks of temporary, partial relief before my symptoms returned.

### 2. Complex Imaging Evidence
*   **BCBSND Policy Criterion:** 
    > *"complex imaging studies (i.e., CT, MRI, X-ray) demonstrate at least ONE of the following at each impacted level being considered for the fusion: 
    >  Herniated nucleus pulposus
    >  Spondylosis (i.e., presence of osteophytes)
    >  Visible loss of disc height compared to adjacent levels with resultant foraminal stenosis"*
*   **Clinical Mapping:** 
    *   An MRI of my cervical spine performed on June 26, 2026, clearly demonstrates a **"C5-C6 disc herniation with severe right foraminal narrowing and C6 nerve root compression."** This imaging definitively establishes both a **"Herniated nucleus pulposus"** and **"resultant foraminal stenosis"** at the targeted surgical level, satisfying this criterion.

### 3. Physical Exam and Imaging Correlation
*   **BCBSND Policy Criterion:** 
    > *"physical examination findings and imaging studies correlate with each level being considered for the fusion"*
*   **Clinical Mapping:** 
    *   My physical examination findings perfectly correlate with the C5-C6 level imaged on my MRI. Specifically, I exhibit a focal neurological deficit consisting of radicular pain, numbness, and weakness in my right thumb and index finger (which is the classic clinical presentation of a C6 radiculopathy). Additionally, Dr. Marchetti's physical examination noted positive provocative testing on the affected right side, correlating directly with the severe right foraminal narrowing and C6 nerve root compression documented on the C5-C6 MRI.

### Additional Clinical Factors
I am an ideal candidate for this surgical intervention. I have no active infections, no untreated substance use issues, a healthy body mass index (BMI) of 29, and I am a non-smoker, which minimizes surgical risks and supports optimal bone healing post-fusion.

### Conclusion
My clinical record demonstrates 14 months of progressive neck and arm pain, 8 weeks of exhaustive physical therapy, unsuccessful medical management, and clear diagnostic imaging showing a herniated disc and foraminal stenosis that perfectly correlates with my physical deficits. I meet every criterion outlined in BCBSND Medical Policy S-9004-02.

I request that you immediately overturn this denial and authorize CPT code 22551 so that I can proceed with this medically necessary, corrective surgery with Dr. Marchetti. 

Please find attached my physical therapy discharge records, MRI report dated June 26, 2026, and Dr. Marchetti's clinical evaluation notes. If you require any additional information, please contact me at [Patient Phone Number] or Dr. Marchetti’s office at [Provider Phone Number].

Thank you for your prompt reconsideration of this request.

Sincerely,

Rowan Delgado  
[Patient Address]  
Member ID: W865123628
